display.title: Episode 444: The Strange Beggar, Chapter 2 (Selichos)
display.summary_short: Before Selichos, Uncle Yossi explains the blessing of the last Shabbos of the year; in the story, Rabbi Yisrael disguises himself as a beggar.
display.summary_long: Broadcast a few days before Selichos 5750. Uncle Yossi explains that on the last Shabbos of the year Hashem gives a blessing for the whole coming year, as the Zohar teaches that Shabbos is the source of blessing for all the days, which is why we say Tehillim early that morning. Selichos begin after midnight that Shabbos night, so the blessing reaches us in full with a clean record. After the Hakochainik march and the pushka, two young brothers visiting from Madrid, Spain recite the Shema. Story time continues 'The Strange Beggar': Rabbi Yisrael disguises himself in shabby clothes and goes from door to door in the town that wants him as rabbi, but every door is slammed in his face. Saddened, he decides that these people need a teacher all the more, and he thinks up a new plan to teach them a lesson. A teenage listener's letter thanks Tzivos Hashem for eight years of programs and asks about the story-time tapes. The show ends with a Selichos reminder and Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: Welcome guests and give tzedakah gladly; and a leader helps people improve instead of giving up on them.

date.note: Selichos begin 'this coming Shabbos night', the last Shabbos of the year, with Rosh Hashanah the following week: the Tuesday before is 21 Elul 5750. Candle time 6:49 fits mid-September.

sources_cited.note: From Shabbos all the days are blessed.
